title: Japanese 11-Year-Old Wins Esports Gold Medal
paragraphs: An 11-year-old boy from Japan has won a gold medal in esports at the Asian Games, making history in the process.

On September 26, 2026, Yuki Kurihara, an elementary school student, won the Puyo Puyo Champions event at the Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan. Puyo Puyo is a puzzle game in which players drop colorful blobs and try to clear them from the screen.

In the final, Kurihara faced Kang Dong-shin of South Korea. Although Kurihara fell behind at the start of the match, he went on to win 10-2. Earlier, in the quarterfinal, he played Justine Koh Mun June of Singapore. In the semifinal, he beat Tanarak Wongkitikun of Thailand, who is 28 years old, 10-1.

Kurihara was the youngest competitor at the Games, and he is believed to be the youngest gold medalist in Asian Games history. However, according to one news agency, there are no public records of the youngest medalists. His victory was also Japan's first esports gold medal at the Asian Games, which Japan was hosting.

After his win, Kurihara said he was really happy and described his medal as "beautiful, shiny and heavy." His opponent, Kang, praised him, saying that his technical skills and accuracy were incredible.

According to Japanese media, Kurihara practices for eight hours a day, but he still keeps up his grades at school. Earlier in 2026, he became the first elementary school student to receive a professional license from the Japan Esports Union.
Esports first became an official medal event at the Asian Games three years earlier, in Hangzhou, China. The sport is very popular with audiences in Japan.
Kurihara was not the only young star at the Games. For example, 13-year-old Yu Zidi of China won three gold medals in swimming.
